policy.failure_logging: every request, including failures, is in requests.jsonl

sources.notes: AccessGUDID (NLM) /api/v3/devices/lookup?di= returns the GUDID record as JSON. GUDID is the upstream database that openFDA /device/udi.json re-publishes: the same DI yields the same publicDeviceRecordKey on both interfaces, so they are ONE evidence item, not two. GUDID publish_date is a real per-record first-publication date; public_version_date is a version stamp and must never be used as the first-publication date.

Health Canada publishes a documented JSON/XML API (no key) for MDALL: company / licence / device / deviceidentifier. `first_licence_status_dt` (licence) and `first_licence_dt` (device) are the only real dates; `last_refresh_dt` is a database refresh stamp and `end_date` is a cancellation date, so neither may be used as the first-publication date. The deviceidentifier endpoint takes a real UDI-DI, which is an official bridge to GUDID for devices sold in both markets.

CT.gov v2 returned 200 JSON with `studies`, `totalCount` and `nextPageToken`.  `statusModule.studyFirstPostDateStruct.date` is the first-public-registration date and is the only defensible `source_public_at`; `startDateStruct.date` is the study start and must not be substituted.  `sponsorCollaboratorsModule.leadSponsor.name` is the deterministic company field (identity.CompanyIndex.resolve).

Crossref REST returned 200 JSON with `message.items` for query, bibliographic query and filter calls.  Works give DOI, `published-online`/`published-print` (must be kept apart), `created`/`deposited` (registration clocks, never publication dates), `funder[]` with award numbers and `relation`.  `mailto=` puts us in the polite pool.

CTIS exposes an unauthenticated JSON API at `https://euclinicaltrials.eu/ctis-public-api` (`POST /search`, `GET /retrieve/{ctNumber}`), used by its own public search front end. It is not a formally versioned/documented developer API, so the register records `api_available: PARTIAL`; `ctNumber` is the authoritative identifier and `decisionDate`/`publishDate` are the clock candidates (first public visibility).

TED Search API v3 answered anonymous POST queries with real notices (no key). notice-type separates contract notices (cn-standard, 2.95M) from contract award notices (can-standard, 2.86M), so tender publication and award publication are distinguishable. The award winner is NOT in the search index: winner-name / winner-partname come back null even for a 2024 medical award notice, so an award→supplier link cannot be built from the search API; a full-text FT~ query finds notices that merely mention a firm. CPV is a category, not a device ID. The ted.europa.eu web host serves a 'Human Verification' challenge (notice_xml_on_web_host, bulk_downloads_page), so anonymous bulk XML download is NOT verified.

Europe PMC REST returned 200 JSON with `resultList.result` and `hitCount`. `resultType=core` supplies `firstPublicationDate`, `firstIndexDate`, DOI/PMID/PMCID, `authorList[].affiliation`, `grantsList` and `dbCrossReferenceList` - enough for DOI-based cross-source de-duplication, author-affiliation company matching and grant-number linking.  `firstIndexDate` is an ingestion clock, not publication.
Comext dissemination API is open and keyless; real 2023 DE/US HS9018 values returned. Correct base path is /api/comext/... and dimensions are reporter/partner/product/flow.

Greenhouse boards-api answers anonymously for a control token, so the endpoint works; the five target firms were tested by their likely board tokens and the ones that resolved are: none. A 404 is the API's answer for 'no such board', not a network failure. Token guessing was capped at 6 requests; absence here means 'not a Greenhouse customer under these tokens', not 'no hiring data exists'.

Lever postings API answers anonymously for a control token, so the endpoint works; target-firm tokens that resolved: none. Lever returns createdAt (source publication time) per posting, which is what the hiring evidence needs, but only for companies that actually use Lever.

NIH RePORTER v2 is POST-only and needs no key: `POST /v2/projects/search` with a `criteria` object returned 200 JSON and `results`.  Grants carry `project_num`, `project_start_date` (event_at), `award_notice_date` (approximate public-visibility clock of the award record), `organization.org_name` (company field) and `agency_ic_*`.  The same grant must not be counted twice when several fiscal-year queries overlap.

Probes the Graph v1 `researchProducts` endpoint and the legacy `search/publications` endpoint.  OpenAIRE aggregates repository copies, so the same paper appears many times: only DOI-based canonical keys may be counted as independent evidence.

OpenAlex answered every query with 200 and real work objects, no key required. Works carry `publication_date` (first online publication), `created_date` (metadata ingestion - NOT a publication clock), DOI/PMID ids, author institutions and `grants`. Use the polite pool (`mailto=`) and never treat `created_date` as public visibility.

device/510k returns real records (JSON, meta.results.total present). No key needed. `decision_date` is the clearance decision date; FDA publishes no per-record first-publication timestamp, so source_public_at may only be derived from the decision date and must be flagged as coarse evidence, never used as a published-on date.

The product-code dictionary is small (~7k codes) and is the join key between a 510(k)/PMA submission and a device family, so it is a cheap full pull (<=8 pages at limit=1000) rather than a windowed collection.

5/5 checks ok; MAUDE reports returned; nested device.manufacturer_d_name is required (bare name -> 404); Medtronic family meta.total=3360860; date_received buckets=9619 summing to 3360860. Passive-surveillance caveat recorded.

device/pma returns PMA originals and supplements; a supplement is a distinct record (pma_number + supplement_number) under the same approval. Same date caveat as 510(k): decision_date is an event date, not a publication date.
4/4 checks ok; limit=2 returned real device-recall records; Medtronic phrase search meta.total=1932; date fields are event_date_initiated/posted (report_date absent).

Registration & listing is establishment-level (who may distribute what), not product-level; it carries k_number/pma_number per establishment which makes it a registrant bridge, but it must not be counted as a second clearance record.

E-utilities esearch/esummary returned 200 JSON.  No key is needed at 3 req/s; the connector declares `tool`/`email` for a better politeness tier and stays below the limit with a 1.2 s minimum interval.  esummary gives `pubdate`/`epubdate` (coarse when only a year/month is published), DOI and PMC id for de-duplication.

Probed unauthenticated.  429 responses mean the shared un-keyed pool is exhausted, not that the API is private: a free API key raises the limit.  Recorded honestly as rate-limited (see PROBE_RESULT.json); no connector ships without a verified 2xx record.

UK Find a Tender serves anonymous OCDS 1.1 release packages. Releases are tagged/staged, so a tender release and its award release are separate objects with separate publication dates — exactly the layering needed. The feed has no keyword parameter; a company-targeted query only exists as the HTML search page, so firm-level retrieval cannot use the OCDS API alone.
Open OData, no key. Publishes named UK traders x CN8 commodity x month (presence only, no values) plus aggregate OTS values.
Public preview endpoint works keyless (HS9018/9022/9402 all 200, 278 partner rows seen); full /data/v1 endpoint is 401 without a subscription key.

USAspending v2 is anonymously readable: award search is POST-only and returned real award rows without an API key; award detail exposes Date Signed and Period of Performance separately, so the publication date and the performance date are not the same field. recipient_search_text is a token search (it returns CHANGE HEALTHCARE for 'GE HealthCare'), so recipient hits are candidates until identity resolution confirms them.

NLM publishes GUDID release files: daily / weekly / monthly change sets and a full release. Daily files are small enough to download inside the protocol budget and carry an explicit 'Date Created' + record count + MD5, which gives a true per-batch publication clock. The full release is far above the 8 MB cap.

api.fda.gov/download.json is the official export manifest: per-endpoint `total_records` and an `export_date` that is a genuine snapshot clock (unlike the API's per-endpoint `last_updated`). One export partition was downloaded and parsed, which is what distinguishes VERIFIED_BULK_DOWNLOAD from a doc claim.

Only the two endpoints the public site itself exposes were requested. Whatever the outcome, no anti-bot or login mechanism was bypassed; if the search path is not machine-readable the register records China procurement as unverified rather than as 'available with caveats'.

CORDIS publishes no documented, versioned developer API.  Its public search front end calls an unauthenticated JSON endpoint (`https://cordis.europa.eu/search/en?format=json`). Probed it directly; if it returns JSON project records the source is a public-query API (undocumented, so `api_available: PARTIAL`), the data being CC-BY 4.0.  No scraping of rendered HTML and no request amplification.
no openFDA shortage endpoint (404 confirmed); HTML list parsed into 6 shortage rows + 236 discontinuance rows, 242 schema-v1 evidence records. Listing date is the only published clock.

no openFDA endpoint; ialist.html parsed into 154 import alerts with number/type/publish-date/name, 154 schema-v1 evidence records; device industry group lists 19 sub-industries. Index has no company column, so firm-level linkage is UNKNOWN.

consultas.anvisa.gov.br is an Angular SPA; its JSON API answers 401/403 without a bearer token issued by the ANVISA login flow, so device registrations require a registered account. No anonymous machine interface was found.
OPS 3.2 rejects unauthenticated calls (403 Fair Use policy); OAuth2 free registration, 4GB/month.

EUDAMED's public SPA loads, but every public data endpoint answers HTTP 429 with an explicit policy message telling automated clients to use the official EUDAMED data API instead of scraping. That machine API lives on the DG SANTE developer portal and needs registered credentials, so the source is reachable only after registration; the public endpoints are off-limits to this study by the operator's own instruction (probe stores the exact message).
GCP project + OAuth + billing account required (401 anonymous); 1TB/month free query allowance but not free of setup.

SAM.gov documents api_key as mandatory for /opportunities/v2/search. Unauthenticated requests (with and without a bogus key) were answered by the istio-envoy gateway with 404 and an empty body - not the 401/403 the protocol expects, so the registration requirement is a DOCUMENTED fact while the live observation only proves the endpoint refuses anonymous callers. No key was registered.
Keyless calls return HTTP 200 with an HTML 'Missing Key' page; free API key required. Data is HS-code aggregate only.
api.uspto.gov returns 401 Unauthorized without X-API-KEY; free key from developer portal.
bulkdata.uspto.gov no longer resolves; ODP bulk/dataset API requires X-API-KEY (401). Zero bytes of bulk data downloaded.
No open API; PCT data products are subscription-gated; UI not scraped (policy).
Quote-based commercial BoL data (Descartes); documented URL in SOURCE_ID_INDEX is 404, live page is /datamyne.
Paid-only BoL vendor; public pricing page read ($159, $183, $1999, $2,198, $229, $359).
API is institutional-subscription only (terms page quote); 401 without token; redistribution restricted.
Sales-negotiated S&P subscription; no public price list; buyer/supplier BoL + corporate hierarchy under contract.

NMPA answers HTTP 412 with a JavaScript anti-bot challenge (a dynamic <meta> token that must be solved by running obfuscated script) before any content is served. Solving or replaying that challenge is a WAF bypass, which the collection protocol forbids, so the source is recorded as blocked rather than retried.
robots.txt disallows /search?q (the only useful query path) and the JSON API paths; no data request made. Policy block.

Every request to tga.gov.au timed out (90-120 s) or was reset by the remote end from this host, so the ARTG could not be verified either way. During reconnaissance the ARTG path returned an Akamai bot-manager proof-of-work interstitial (`bm-verify` / `/_sec/verify`); that observation is recorded here but was NOT reproduced inside this logged probe, so the probe status is UNAVAILABLE, not BLOCKED_BY_POLICY.

sources.notes: stats.customs.gov.cn returns HTTP 412 anti-automation; no API, no anonymous bulk; portal has no query interface.

The NMPA UDI portal serves a JSP/JS shell whose data calls are session-bound and undocumented; no public machine interface was found and the documented paths did not return records. Recorded as unavailable rather than guessed at.

Corporate careers pages were fetched one request per firm (plus robots.txt where present), no crawling. An HTML page that mentions jobs is not a job feed: the register records how many firms answer HTML and whether any machine-readable vacancy payload is present, and does not claim a hiring dataset from these pages.

PMDA's device database (kikiSearch) is a legacy servlet that renders an HTML form and only answers a form POST; a GET with query parameters returns the empty form again. No documented API and no bulk release exist, so there is no machine-readable path for this study. The pages themselves are reachable, so this is 'no machine interface', not 'no data'.
Documented host search.patentsview.org is NXDOMAIN; api host now serves an ODP-branded SPA. Retired/absorbed into uspto_open_data_portal.

SBIR.gov documents an unauthenticated awards API, but on every probe the API host answered 403 Forbidden (also to a plain browser-style fetch) while the official /api page carries a maintenance notice.  This is not a registration requirement: the documented endpoints need no key.  Recorded UNAVAILABLE (documented API temporarily refusing anonymous service) with the evidence preserved, not as a working source.

GOV.UK search for MHRA device material returns only *guidance* (how a manufacturer registers a device), not a public register of licensed products: the UK has no searchable public medical-device register equivalent to MDALL/EUDAMED/GUDID. There is therefore no product-level UK regulatory dataset to collect.
SPA-only site, no discoverable API; www.usitc.gov 403. Registered web UI only; redundant with Census for aggregate purposes.

ICTRP is a search portal over national registries, with no public machine API.  The probe records the portal responses but they are HTML forms, not queryable records, so the source is recorded UNAVAILABLE for programmatic collection.  The registries it indexes (CT.gov, CTIS, ChiCTR, ...) are collected directly instead.

No vendor-neutral public API exists; each employer exposes its own tenant. Per-employer JSON endpoints answering: none. TLS hostname-mismatch failures: ['phenom_host_medtronic'] — TLS verification was not disabled to work around them. A working tenant endpoint is site-specific, not a generalisable job-postings API.

sources.notes: OCDS is a data standard plus a publisher registry, not a record publisher: the official site documents the release/record model and lists publishers, and has no homogeneous record API of its own. Status is NOT_TESTED on purpose - calling a documentation site 'verified' would be a category error. Actual OCDS records were verified through a real publisher instead (uk_find_a_tender, OCDS 1.1).
